notes.title: Update to Previous Build about Music
notes.content:
Doing a wild thing and defaulting the new music tracks to "on" for the main build!  If you want to go back to original music, you can still toggle it at the main menu with the "]" key.

I'll be adding some more tracks throughout the week, and doing a big full post about this when the whole thing is wrapped up.  Although there's a good chance even after that there will be some new tracks added as well, hop in and check out the stuff!

notes.title: Secret Cheat for a Music Test
notes.content:
Hey everyone, as some loyal fans have pointed out, the gameplay music (particularly the non "chase" gameplay theme) is a bit too tension oriented and less action oriented which sets the wrong pace for the game. This potentially sets incorrect expectations of the gameplay from the start, and fails to live up to the action later in the game as well.

I'm testing a new gameplay track I've composed for the game, to see if the higher action / rock feel works better in the context.

By default the original music will play, but on the main menu screen before starting a run if you press "]" on your keyboard, you'll see a popup that you're using the new gameplay music. Now when you enter a mission you'll hear a new higher tempo and action track to play to!

Right now:
- There is only 1 new track (I think probably having 2 or 3 that rotate each level will ultimately feel better)
- The mini boss and boss music will likely be "next", and I think each one should have it's own track in the end but they will share one for mow
- The towns are still using the default gameplay music, so it's a bit of a mis-fit in towns, but I'll probably tackle that one after the boss track (before the alternate gameplay track / tracks)
- The map may receive one too, so it's not using the same as the title screen, but that's my lowest priority for now, the gameplay music is the first one I want to tackle

Try it out, let me know what you think!

notes.title: Some dead-end Consolation Prizes
notes.content:
Quick change to itemization in levels to help with the dead end problem.  There are still some dead ends possible, and I think this is good for the risk / reward of exploration and weighing that against the escalation time.

But now collectibles are a bit more likely to spawn in rooms that don't have objective's in them. It's now up to you to decide if you want to fully explore levels and risk the timer, or stick to the objectives only. This is an indirect buff to escalation time perks as well, since those will now result in a slightly high loot collection rate.

Additionally, bosses and mini-bosses have an additional item drop added to them to balance this out a little and make the loot-splosions more exciting.

notes.title: Feedback improvements for Combos and Consumeables
notes.content:
Combo:
- Increased time between hits to feel better when you cross the gap to keep the combo running
- Added a combo timer bar to visual show how quickly it is decaying
- Fixed the alpha fade to be less linear and grouped to the low end of the bar

Consumeables:
- Fixed a bug with some data tracking that could result in consumables not being applied
- Added text to show if a consumable is active when hovering in inventory

notes.title: Small Perk Update
notes.content:
Some quick updates to the "Second Wind" Legendary perk:
- Change from 20 health, to 25% health so it will scale a bit later in game to offset scaled enemy damage
- Add additional invulnerability frames to avoid immediate damage or multihits
- Add a knockback effect to push enemies away
- Add a text toast "Second Wind!" on the player so it's clear what happened

I'm also testing around with some additional visual effects, but these changes make it significantly better to play with and more clear when it happens.

notes.title: Cubed and Dangerous Version 1.5
notes.content: [p]Hey everyone, the game has received quite a bit of renewed attention this year and that's produced a lot of great feedback to help improve the game. Today I've deployed version 1.5 of Cubed and Dangerous to accumulate all of the changes for feedback collected so far. Hope you enjoy the updates![/p][p]Many pieces of feedback were beautifully delivered in Steam Reviews, and remains a great way to support games you love, the steam community and help developers learn and grow. So thank you everyone who has done that so far![/p][p]Here's a high-level summary of what you can find in this new update.[/p][p][/p][h1]Difficulty[/h1][p]Onboarding new players has been an interesting tug-of-war in the realm of difficulty balancing. Some players are finding this game (or other twin stick shooters) for the first time, having been exposed to more survivor likes or bullet heaven games. Others are here because they've played classics like Nuclear Throne / Enter the Gungeon and are looking for some more mayhem.[/p][p]To satisfy players across this spectrum, I've tried to balance the difficulty for early runs while still providing a challenge. The result just hasn't really lived up to what I was looking for.[/p][p]This patch changes the way difficulty works by enabling the challenge mode selector, available on skill selection page before a new run, for all players.[/p][p]This will default to "off" so if you don't see it or just want to jump into your first run, you can still play on a relatively easy difficulty. But if you're a veteran coming in and want a challenge before you've unlocked more end game content, you can now select some of the earlier challenges to significantly ramp things up. The choice is now fully yours! Apologies for not bringing this feature closer to the front of early runs before.[/p][p][/p][h1]Balance[/h1][p]All weapons and tactical items have had a balance pass, and are just too numerous to mention here.  You'll have to try them out and see if things feel better than before. Nothing large and sweeping has been changed because most of the balance in feedback was that things felt pretty good overall, and many builds are viable.[/p][p]Flamethrower weapon classes still received a little bit of a buff, some of the explosives were toned down just a tiny bit since they scale across many different perk selections and strategies. Ammo was increased for a few weapons as well.[/p][p]I am also keeping an eye on ammo in general, potentially could overhaul that entire system if there's enough feedback about it.[/p][p][/p][h1]Stability / Useability[/h1][p]The game has been pretty stable for a while now, no reported crashes in months. So that's been great! There are a few places where some weird behavior was noticed though, so I've taken this opportunity to revamp a bunch of things in the UI to make it more stable:[/p][list][*][p]Escape key on the keyboard was interacting with a few screens in really weird ways[/p][/*][*][p]Unboxing animation didn't call out relics as special items[/p][/*][*][p]Challenge mode selector was sometimes not visible at all (overhauled in the callout above)[/p][/*][*][p]Game title added to main menu[/p][/*][*][p]Cursor improvements to not lose it on most levels (keeping an eye on this one too)[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy AI improvements, bosses will be a little more responsive to the player and their actions[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a small bug that could sometimes result in the wrong items unboxing[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed unlock all buttons so they actually work more often now (all the time ideally)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]More and more[/h1][p]There are also a ton of smaller bugs around weird interactions that have all been cleared up.  Places where spamming buttons could cause strange UI or interaction behavior, shops could have glitched out inventories, etc. Safe to say, if you experienced some odd behavior in a run in the past, there's a good chance it was in the huge bug list tackled this time around.[/p][p][/p][h1]Feedback[/h1][p]As always, I'd love to hear your feedback. The players are instrumental in this process, both from the perspective of supporting this game as well as impacting the development of future games (Sheep for the Stars being one of the more recent games released). I want to hear what you think, what you'd like to see, what you already love, why it's your favorite game, or anything else you want to share.[/p][p]Reach out through the communities here, Steam Reviews, Discord Server, or the new Ace High Arcade Subreddit. I try to make sure I read every single review or post to know what I'm doing well and what can be improved.[/p]

notes.title: Econ and Itemization Improvement Patch
notes.content: [p]Hey everyone, I've just made some significant changes to aspects of the game's economy and itemization today. This set of changes is focused around improving the shop experience, balancing some aspects around economy focused builds, and some other new changes![/p][p][/p][h1]What Isn't Changing[/h1][p]In a previous news post I had mentioned that vendor inventories were going to change. I explored some ways to improve it and did a few rounds of playtesting with the changes, and players felt that it reduced some of the surprise in shops.[/p][p]Therefore, in this patch today I've focused on improving the town / shop experience with some of the other changes and left the specific inventory changes to a future patch to give it some more time to bake with playtesting. Don't worry though, the other changes in combination with each other are a significant improvement in the experience.[/p][p][/p][h1]Shops and Towns[/h1][p]Towns have been reduced in size variance, limiting the number of rooms generated significantly. This will reduce the pressure players feel to check out every vendor before making a purchase or choosing to spend money on the forge. There's still some variance in room selection between single and multi vendor layouts, but this keeps the concentration of options closer together for less travel time. I'll still be exploring some new layouts with a room update in the future, to make this aspect of the change even better as it evolves further.[/p][p]Shops specifically have received a couple specific buffs:[/p][list][*][p]Common and Rare items in shop have a quality (star level) bonus when appearing, making them more exciting to find and helping bridge the gap for builds focused on forging vs high rarity item hunting[/p][/*][*][p]Prices have moved a little closer together to compensate for this change, now the choice between a shiny legendary or a 3 star Rare item is much more difficult to make.  Do you choose immediate power in the high level Rare, or do you invest in the future at the cost of short term gain?[/p][/*][*][p]Perk boxes in shops have been fixed so their prices reflect similar effects as the item costs, making re-rolling for legendary perks a valid late game econ payoff[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Foiled Items[/h1][p]Foil items have received a bit more love in this patch. Foil items represent an increase in maximum item quality at the cost of additional gold (or forge resources). A Foiled Common Pistol for example receives double the effects of all augments rolled on the item. Theoretically a 5 star version of this item would behave like a 10 star one (in actuality it's a little less, but still close to double).[/p][p]The issue with foiled items previously was that their cost was too high for this utility, making it optimal to just pass on them or sell them to use the money + interest for better effects later. To fix this, the cost for foiled items (and their forge costs) have been reduced to make them more enticing and exciting to find.[/p][p]Additionally, the effect on the cards was a bit too subtle to see and there weren't many places where the game would draw your attention to the fact the item was foiled to begin with. I've increased the contrast on the effect, brought a little bit of HDR in to the shine, improved the animation, and added a text hint when inspecting foiled items. This should help them stand out more and be exciting to stumble upon.[/p][p][/p][h1]Items and General Econ[/h1][p]A small gold boost has been added to the option to skip a perk during selection. The original value was initially too low, making it almost certainly always optimal to take a perk instead of passing on them. With a bit of an increase to this value, the choice is now much harder. Especially early in the game with a class that has a low starting gold count (looking at you, Mutant) skipping an early perk might help get your econ back on track. The new values have scored much better in playtesting as an option that players are taking more often.[/p][p]Since towns now have less vendors, I've also reduced forge cost slightly to compensate. It was probably too accessible previously any way, so the change is subtle to hopefully meet in the middle a little. It's not possible to forge as much as you could before, but also hasn't been reduced too far in effectiveness. I'll keep an eye on it going forward, but in high level test runs it's still possible to optimize your econ for a heavy forge build and still generate very significant power.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks again everyone for playing, happy Steam Summer Sale Shopping to all! If you have any feedback or just want to chat about the game, feel free to hit up any of the social channels.[/p]

notes.title: Town Improvements Coming Soon
notes.content: [p]A Cubed and Dangerous Update is coming very soon. It may be available during the first couple days of the Summer Sale if I can manage it, but there are a few bugs with the update that I don't want to risk destabilizing the game over.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What's Coming[/b][/p][p]The patch is focused on making the global shop, town map nodes, and vendor in-level spawns more impactful. There might also be some other goodies added along with it if I can get them working in time.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Global Shop[/b][/p][p]The global shop, and town shops, will be changed to provide a quality and rarity boost to items. You'll still be able to find of the common items in the shops, but they will be compensated with higher quality (star rating) to make even the lower level gear more exciting to see in shops. To compensate for the balance change, the cost of items in the shop may be increased a little after more testing. This should help support shop-based strategies and build-around decisions by giving a higher weighted payout.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Town Map Nodes[/b][/p][p]Towns are generally too sprawling in space, and vendors are difficult to compare against. Optimal town strategy requires visiting every vendor before buying anything, which can slow gameplay down a bit too much.[/p][p]To fix this, towns will be changed to relatively fixed sizes (2 to 3 rooms) and vendors will be assigned roles to make it easier to make decisions. eg: A weapons vendor for hand weapons and tacticals, a gear vendor for hats/armor/boots/belts, and a utility vendor for heals or perks.[/p][p]This should make it easier to target types of items you're looking for, and make town encounters a bit more streamlined.[/p][p]These vendors will all also receive the weighting improvements mentioned for the global shop, to make their inventories more exciting to browse.[/p][p][/p][p][b]In Level Vendors[/b][/p][p]These are going to be more rare than they currently are (potentially 33% of their current spawn rate) and will include a larger boost to the rarity weighting. The scarcity plus additional rarity should help make them more exciting when they show up. Additionally this will make it possible to do even more interesting things in the future with rare room spawns.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Next Fest[/b][/p][p]Thanks everyone for hanging out with me, blasting cubed, exploring the desert, and even checking out Sheep for the Stars during Next Fest. I've been busy trying to get that demo polished up for the event and fixing some feedback coming from it. But the next little while will see some more structured time working between both games.[/p][p]If you want to follow along with development, or chat about anything, stop by the Steam Community / Reddit / Discord / YouTube.[/p]

notes.title: Balance and Bug Update + News
notes.content:
Hey Everyone,

I've been busy working on some of the core mechanics and fixes for Sheep for the Stars ahead of Steam Next Fest, and have been accumulating some changes and updates to Cubed and Dangerous that just went live.

Thank you all for your continued support and feedback on the games.  This support and feedback is instrumental in ensuring this game can reach towards it's utmost potential. I really sincerely appreciate all of it, keep it coming!

[b]General Balance Updates
[/b]- Reduce spike damage from Living Bomb enemies by 10% in lower difficulty levels
- Fixed an issue with level generation that could result in extended mission playtimes (bug fix impacts balance)

[b]Weapon Balance Updates
[/b]Based on feedback from players along with some distributed playtesting and modeling, some of your favorite weapons were found to be a bit under the general expected effectiveness bar for weapons in the game. While it's certainly expected that not all weapons will be direct 1 to 1 comparable in terms of damage output, some were falling a bit too far behind.

- Flamethrower / Plasmathrower: Damage increased by 10%
- Spiral Laser / Honed Laser: Damage increased by 15%, ammo slightly reduced (only has an effect on large ammunition perk builds, about 3% overall)
- Chaingun: Damage increased 15%
- Magnum: Damage increased 5%

I'll keep an eye on how this impacts progression throughout the game, but preliminary testing has made these weapons feel a bit more effective across challenge levels.

[b]Bug Fixes
[/b]- Fixed an issue with controller support that wasn't handling analogue trigger dead zones, should improve UI interactions for gamepad players
- Fix an issue with main menu graphics overlaying during gameplay when spamming buttons at the main menu

[b]Upcoming Updates
[/b]In the next month or so, I'll be looking at the friendly town encounters and looking for some ways to help improve them in the flow of gameplay.  Currently considering:
- Reducing the number of vendors in towns / smoothing over the variance in the number of vendors
- Increasing the quality of items found within vendors
- Potentially adding a new type of vendor

Thanks again everyone for your feedback on the game so far, it's been a blast working alongside a supportive community!

notes.title: Bug Fix: Difficulty Scaling and Smoothing
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Just deployed a quick bug fix to the game.  There was an issue with how difficulty scaling was being applied at cumulative challenge levels below 5.  This fix corrects the calculation, and will make challenge level 0 behave closer to the intended design, but we'll monitor closely to make sure it's not the only issue impacting the early game content.

Specifically, Challenge Level Zero is how the game starts for new players.  Once you complete the campaign, you'll unlock more challenge levels that can be selected when starting a new run (you'll see the option at the bottom of the skill select screen during character select).

This challenge level was incorrectly applying an enemy scale to damage, and health (along with some other stats, secret shhhh).  The bug fix ensures this is not applied on this level, and smoothly ramps up to applying to subsequent levels 1 through 5.  After 5 the built in ramping takes a back seat to the more drastic changes applied during each of the progressive levels, be warned, the challenge will definitely change from there.

If you're played the game before and felt like the first run was far too challenging, give the game another shot!  This fix significantly changes the way enemies behave during introductory runs before you start engaging in recruit collecting or some of the other late game content.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Spring Update Details
notes.content:
Cubed and Dangerous is back! Also, on sale in the Spring Sale so tell your friends!

For new and returning players, there are a lot of changes that have been made over the last week or two to really improve the cubed and dangerous experience. If you've played before or you're thinking of checking it out now, it's a great time!

[b]Steam Achievements[/b]

Cubed and Dangerous now has Steam Achievements! There are 15 in the game now, and a whole new set coming in the next couple of days. The achievements that have been added so far provide some additional challenges around campaign completion, end game content, some fun build-arounds to try, and other replayability focus areas.

Some of these were in the old built in achievement system in the game, but are now fully exposed to Steam. Hopefully in the future the game will be approved for profile inclusion so you can add achievements from the game there as well, fingers crossed!

[b]Difficulty Curve Adjustments[/b]

There's been a larger focus this time around on early game difficulty, new player onboarding and generally ramping down some of the surprise run-end situations that used to arise. There have been a lot of changes in this area so here's a summary list:
[list]
[*] Reduce enemy bullet speed to improve dodging and maneuverability during gameplay
[*] Re-balance enemy health across the board for more satisfying run-and-gun interactions (bosses included)
[*] Improve invincibility frames on hit for better recovery, making intense situations more manageable
[*] Fix issues with friendly-fire from barrels and mission objective explosions
[*] Add more gear drops to early levels, and improving risk-reward for taking on harder (skulled) missions
[/list]

The barrel explosions and mission objectives were interestingly the number 1 cause of early run ending events from playtesting.  The friendly fire was so high, it made it difficulty to maneuver in large firefights while still avoiding barrels.  To make this even worse, enemies could blow up the barrels so the interaction was beyond your control in many situations.  The damage is still present, but has been significantly reduced (over 70% reduction on average).  Now they operate much more closely to other level based traps, impacting pathing and providing additional challenge without feeling unfair.

[b]Gameplay and Playstyle Options[/b]

Cubed and Dangerous was originally designed as a challenging twin stick shooter with heavy build-crafting and roguelike elements. The game remains true to this nature in design, but now has many options in the settings menu for players who are looking to tailor the experience in different directions.

In the settings menu you'll find options for:

[i]Auto Fire Mode[/i] - This option will take over control of firing primary and secondary weapons for you.  This will feel more like a survivor-like game (for those Vampire Survivors / Brotato fans), it will auto aim and fire at nearest enemies.  Your tactical weapon (ultimate:  Right bumper on gamepad, Q key on keyboard) is still a manual fire, as the ammo is often limited and needs to be deployed tactically in most situations.

[i]Link Fire Buttons[/i] - This option links primary and secondary fire buttons together, so pressing either button will result in firing both weapons simultaneously.  This reduces the need to hold multiple triggers while playing, or if using the mouse only requires a single button click.  This one is a nice stopgap for those who want to still aim and control the twin stick combat, but are having trouble keeping up with firing both weapons.

These two options do alter some balance in the game.  Some weapons with lower ammo or energy costs can become more difficult to use if firing automatically, but you can also change the gameplay options at any time through the pause menu if you want to work around the issues with those weapons specifically.

Additionally, there are also some unlock bypass options if you want to get in and try out all the character classes without finishing the campaign a few times first.  You can only access these buttons from the main menu (not the pause menu) because they will impact the current mission's loot rolls, and can have unintended consequences.  You can find them in the "other" tab in the game settings:

[i]Character Unlock[/i] - Unlocks all the locked character classes.  You'll have instant access to all 14 (number 14 is my favorite) on character select when starting a new run.  There's no way to undo this, other than deleting all of your save data and starting over completely.  So if you enjoy the grind and exploration, don't click.  But if you want maximum content immediately, enjoy!

[i]Item Unlock[/i] - Unlocks all items in the game.  This bypasses the unlock events for defeating act bosses, and will put all possible items into the item pool from the start.  You'll still need to find and equip them to have them discovered in the collection, but will have maximum item variety in every run.  Like the character unlock, this is also irreversible.

[b]Pacing tweaks[/b]

Additionally, the total escalation timer pool has been increased for all levels (roughly 30% total time increase across the board) to allow for more leeway when taking on missions before the Enforcers show up and make things difficult for you.  It's still intended for you to try to complete objectives as quickly as possible, so follow those objective arrows or minimap icons to get things completed quickly!

Heist level final timers have increased as well.  Roughly 3 to 5 seconds additional time per generated room in the level.  Heists were a little too difficult for new players in the early game, and when populations become very large in the late game the timer was still fairly limiting causing more surprising run ends.

Scout mission objectives (those radar dish installations) have had their total HP reduced by around 30%.  Early game they were too bullet-spongy, which dragged the quick pacing of the game down a little.  In the late game they scale with enemies, so they do become more difficult to take down while avoiding the defending squads.  The goal with this change was to help make the early game feel more streamlined while gearing up.

Thanks everyone for the support so far, hope you have fun with the updates and get a chance to dive in!  Still love to hear all your feedback, so hope in the [url=https://discord.com/invite/VUJsGEYu6C]Discord Channel[/url] to connect or drop any feedback and suggestions there.  Additionally, you can email us or join the email list on [url=https://www.acehigharcade.com/]The Ace High Arcade Website[/url] to stay up to date on updates for this and other games.  Including announcements, giveaways, and more (email frequency less than 1 a month).

notes.title: Control Auto Detection Bug Fix
notes.content:
A quick update to provide a workaround for some players who have had issues with control interference.

Some players have reported bugs around not being able to click on items in the menu and progress to gameplay. After some digging it has been discovered that some gamepads or other peripherals that are reporting [i]as[/i] gamepads can cause issues with the controls auto selection in the game.

We've added a workaround that detects whether controls have switched between devices too many times in a short period, and then we turn off auto select for that session and force keyboard/mouse controls.

You'll see a pop up slide in from the left side of the screen that looks like this one:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/54c905d43550b90e21cc8714a99eabc554a833fe.jpg[/img]

The main cause of this is having a gamepad connected that may have some analog stick drift, or has accelerometers with lower accuracy and constant jitter (two things we've been able to test).

So far this hasn't had an effect on gamepad player, and if you have one connected we do highly recommend you play with gamepad since it's way more fun that way.  Long term we'll add some options to permanently disable auto select and force a chosen control device, but we also want to make sure this doesn't end up locking players out of the game completely so we want to test that a lot more.

Let us know if you run into any other issues, or if this change doesn't help in your case. It's difficult to test too many hardware differences ourselves so input from players really helps.

notes.title: Early Game Difficulty Improvements
notes.content:
Quick difficulty / balance patch today to help with some of the new player onboarding.  If you've played the game previously and found it too difficulty or punishing, definitely give this patch a try.

Some things that were changed:
- Increased escalation time pool, more time to explore levels and learn the ropes
- Increased Escape Timer in Heist missions, a little more leeway when going for max loot
- When escalation is full / out of time, reduced Enforcer initial damage and attack speed
- Increase number of early game rewards to jump start progression
- Reduce enemy projectile speed across all enemy types to make dodging more effective

The game is still quite difficult and the challenge levels will revert some of the changes listed above.  So there are still lots of additional modifiers to enjoy along with late game builds and recruits.

Tip: We've made it so you have more time to complete levels, but Enforcers are still extremely deadly.  Be sure to not take the extra time for granted too much.  Happy cube blasting!

(Be sure to share us some screen shots of your procedural recruits when you complete your runs!)

notes.title: Upcoming patch focused on Controls
notes.content:
Quick update:  Working on an upcoming patch to address some of the edge cases around auto-detection for gamepad and mouse/kb. Let us know if you're running into any controls issues and we can try to tackle some of them in this update.

*The game does use Steam Input so hopefully that is covering the majority of players.

Thanks for playing, happy Steam Next Fest everyone!

notes.title: Now with more Survivor-like Spice
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Quick update to the game has been added as an experimental feature / option in the settings menu to enable a survivor-like control scheme with auto-aim and auto-fire.

We've received feedback from the community that it would be nice to have this as an option, and in an effort to support as many players as possible we definitely agree!

[b]Full Game and Demo have both received this update![/b]

The option has been added to the settings menu in an experimental fashion for now, and currently have it defaulted to off so if you're looking for this feature be sure to head over there turn it on to play around. Additionally there's also a "link fire mode" option as well, which combines primary and secondary fire into one button if you're looking to retain the manual aiming but want to reduce the button requirements. Options for everyone!

Of course, Cubed and Dangerous is still a challenging twin-stick shooter at it's core so there's very likely going to be some balance inconsistencies when playing with auto fire and auto aim.  Some weapons will be much better than they used to be on manual aim and some other weapons will be worse. Energy weapons in particular are likely to be impacted the most, as you'll no longer be able to time your energy usage very well.  But the option can be toggled off during gameplay, so you can also choose to switch back and forth between modes as much as you'd like while playing.

Thanks for your support so far, we've had a literal blast making this game and working with the feedback from the community. Keep the feedback coming, and if you have any issues at all don't hesitate to hit us up on the discord server.

(More to come from us very very soon as well)

Happy cubed destruction to all!

notes.title: Optimization Patch 3.4
notes.content:
Hey Everyone,

While trying to debug some recent issues with performance on Steam Deck, we've found some areas for optimization that will help improve performance on a larger variety of setups.

Specifically, older generation video cards are now better supported with our shader pipeline. Here's a quick summary of the fixes included in todays patch:
[list]
[*] Fixed issue with offscreen buffers that were much larger than needed
[*] Reduce oversampling on outline and lighting shaders, 2x perf boost overall
[*] Fixed issues with some UI overdraw (significant on Steam Deck), more will be needed
[*] Fixed issues with render textures being updated too frequently
[*] Improved performance for game objects that are offscreen or further from the player
[/list]

Thanks for checking out the game so far!  We've been getting a lot of great feedback, and are always looking for more.

[h2]Quick Update: 2/1/2025[/h2]
We pushed a new Steam Deck patch that adds much needed additional optimization to get a consistent 60+FPS back on the device!

notes.title: Cubed and Dangerous on Steam Deck
notes.content:
Hey everyone! We've been working hard through all of our content patches on continually improving the Cubed and Dangerous experience on Steam Deck and we wanted to collect some of the details up in a post to share with the community.

Overall, the game runs very well on Steam Deck, with fully integrated Steam Input and controls built specifically for the device button layout. Feedback from Steam Deck players has been great so far and helped shape further improvement significantly.

[h2]Steam Support[/h2]
Cubed and Dangerous has been built as a Steam-First title, so it has a seamless experience between PC and Steam Deck.  We added cloud save support that will sync all your game data between devices so you can continue your progress anywhere without the need to run completely different saves. Additionally, your options settings are only stored locally so you can configure your desired settings per platform.

[h2]UI Improvements[/h2]
We've recently completely revamped the UI in the game. The goal with this project was to streamline a lot of the UI flow, improve the look and feel, but also to help with readability on smaller screens and resolutions. The direct impact on Steam Deck is a much easier to read interface, especially on the more complicated screens like inventory and item comparisons.

[h2]Optimizations[/h2]
On PC, games can often get away with less optimal rendering setups, with average desktop graphics cards overcoming the problem with sheer horsepower. With integrated and mobile devices, constraints are much tighter. As we looked at the performance on Steam Deck, we put in a lot of work optimizing the game to support these constraints.

Since launch we've improved average FPS from 45 to well over 90, battery life by almost double and removed many sources of frame hitching and peaks / valleys in performance for the smoothest experience we've had so far.

If you want to squeeze even more performance out of the game, [b]locking it to 60hz in the Steam Deck advanced settings[/b] in testing has gotten us close to 6 hours of constant play time.

[h2]Optimized for Gamepad and Mouse/Keyboard[/h2]
Since the earliest stages of development, Cubed and Dangerous has been built to seamlessly support gamepad and mouse/keyboard controls, allowing users to switch instantly between them with automatic detection.

Being a twin-stick shooter design, the game is also perfectly suited to the Steam Deck gamepad layout.  We also recently added some additional comfort features, so be sure to check out the in game settings for more.

[h2]Feedback[/h2]
We're looking to make this game the best we possibly can on the Steam Deck, and consider the Steam Deck itself as a primary target platform. So if you have any Steam Deck related feedback (or other feedback) we'd love to hear it. Join our discord and help us make this game the best we possibly can.

notes.title: New Feature Preview: Collectable Characters!
notes.content:
We knew a while back that we wanted to do something more interesting with the characters and progression in Cubed And Dangerous and today we're previewing it! Everything previewed here will be available once Content Update 3 lands in a few weeks' time.

Characters in Cubed And Dangerous are going to be extended and turned into Character Classes. Each Character Class will have leveling progression, and on top of that you will collect new characters within each class! These characters can have all sorts of new abilities, special modifiers, better stats, extra gear and weapons, or start their runs with certain Perks or Relics.

Each Character Class will have a starting loadout like the existing characters do, but you will be able to recruit more and more powerful variations on the Character Class as you go, each with near-infinitely variable strengths and drawbacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/52ac9f07ea2cae6692b7cec3f42bfdaa3f3b4a70.png[/img]
These characters are persistent and you'll be able to use them repeatedly. Leveling progress is made within the Class as a whole, such that you never need to lose progression in order to swap from your old character to the new one. (After playtesting, it was clear that it felt pretty bad to progress with a character and then have to sacrifice that progress the moment you found a new upgraded character.)

When can you recruit these new more powerful characters? After some more playtesting, we also found that it was counterintuitive to be given a new character at some point in the middle of a campaign. When someone got offered a new and better character, they'd have a decision - "Do I finish this run before I can start playing with the new character, and thus I don't get to use the cool character I just found? Or do I start a new run and throw away my current progress?" This situation always felt like you were giving something up.

To resolve this, characters are recruited at the most opportune moment - when you complete the campaign and are presented with the option of continuing into the Infinite Desert. If you found a character you prefer, you can begin a new run immediately without missing out on any completion benefits.

There was another question that came up in testing - what if I am only playing one character? If I can recruit a character from any Character Class, well, I mostly don't get something I want. I can't grind directly for an upgrade to my current character, since I'm always getting flooded with other characters. But, if the character you got was always from your current Character Class, you'd never have any incentive to try another class because you were locked into the one you were playing, which was already significantly upgraded and probably always your strongest playable character.

To solve this - when you recruit a new character, you'll actually recruit two at once! You'll recruit a new character in your Character Class that is a potential upgrade, so if you want to grind up to maximum power, you can do so; and you'll also recruit a character from a different class, opening up the ability to discover any character variation at any moment, potentially opening new avenues for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/66c4084ce5e631e7094d7d612c937412ed46cd3f.png[/img]
This is also how Character Classes are unlocked now. Completing the campaign will give you a new character of a new Class if you haven't unlocked every Class yet. This means that every new character you unlock will be from a new Class until you have seen all the possibilities, and you won't be locked behind random rolling to be able to explore and try every different character.

Finally - we are also including a fully-randomized character, for the masochists and challengers among us!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/e99b2b35013368b78d6276edd8fd00339fe15d8b.png[/img]

We hope you'll enjoy the new content drop and the big new changes to the game. Keep an eye on this feed and Wishlist the game if you want to make sure you see the update launch, we'll post more teasers in the next few days. Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Progress Report - We rebuilt the UI and HUD almost entirely...
notes.content:
One of the major pieces of feedback we’ve gotten over time is that our HUD and Menu UI is just not doing it for people. It was functional and showed useful information, but it was ugly and we wanted to replace it almost entirely. We put this off initially as it was a large forklift, but we got some feedback about it that really pushed us forward:

[list]
[*] “Alright, I gotta say, the UIs are really bad. [...] This is bad. This is the first thing you experience in the video game.”
[*] “This is a graphic design disaster.”
[*] “Geometry Wars has a better UI than this.”
[*] “It’s so ugly.”
[*] “They’ve got the basics down right. It’s just the UI that’s a problem.”
[/list]
We decided to dive head-first into revamping both the in-game HUD and all of the menus. Here are a few examples of what we've done to improve!

[h2]The HUD[/h2]

The new HUD cluster is designed to take up less screen space yet still show all the information from the previous one. The new Escalation bar takes up a lot less screen space, positioned towards the top right, under the minimap.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/8bad1cc8f56b74ee1f0c67d567abae390d7a6078.png[/img]

[h2]The Menus[/h2]

The menus have been entirely thrown out and replaced. This new look is much more sleek.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/9707999bdeca50251311bc17c860482df0125c23.png[/img]

The new character select screen is great! Like the others, almost no trace of the original remains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/5cd828ace8ce919b543ee37e8610bbd63d9af1b4.png[/img]

Even just the Options menu is now less clunky, using a sweet and completely rebuilt tab system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45002193/dcfe91bf2e59dbe8c3a97e5bceaa6f7904c817eb.png[/img]

This is still a work in progress, but these updates are starting to make the game look more and more like what we want it to be. We've still got a few more major updates to share - the next post will showcase the major updates to progression systems that we've been doing. Stay tuned for the post about it next Friday!

notes.title: Content Update 2
notes.content:
We’re now a month since launch, and we’ve had some time to think about what worked and what didn’t about our original vision for Cubed and Dangerous. In the last two weeks, we’ve put together some new content that we hope will elevate the game to the next level!

[h2]Relics[/h2]
We noticed that the game didn’t previously present enough things that would fundamentally change the plans that you made as you progressed through the game. We needed something that altered character construction more strongly and made different runs feel significantly different.

Relics are more strongly build-warping than existing gear and perks, redefining the way that you think about different items and your gameplay. You can now find Relics as part of the loot you encounter, and we’ll even throw in one free Relic when you start each run!

[h2]Campaign Map Overview[/h2]
At the start of each Act, it was customary to peruse all of the different levels in the Act and check all of their risks and rewards. This became a chore, but also showed up a different and much worse problem - once you already know what rewards are in a certain level, the level itself would become much less exciting.

To fix this, we’ve hidden item drops for levels, and crucially, we’ve tied the drops more strongly to the difficulty of a level. You’ll no longer be able to scan all the loot drops ahead in an Act, but to compensate we’ve raised the bar on drops and you will be much more likely to drop valuable loot in any given level, as well as able to tilt the odds in your favor by pathing through harder levels. You’ll also see what loot you get as you find it in the level, giving you a sneak peek if you know what you’re looking at!

[h2]Foil Items[/h2]
We wanted to have more of the “woah that’s a sweet shiny drop” reactions, but also to not make those items run-winning in their own right. Cubed and Dangerous had some form of chase items before, but this was mostly restricted to specific Legendary gear and Legendary Perks. So we added rare special versions of items, and LITERALLY made them shiny.

A foil gear item will double the strength of all the forged modifiers on that item. Foil Relics come with a secondary large upside bonus. Beating the campaign with an item will also grant a small chance for future drops of that item to be foiled as well!

[h2]Friend Leaderboards[/h2]
You can now compete against your friends for the title of Most Dangerous Cube! Steam’s Friend Leaderboards feature powers a new button on the main menu. See who can get furthest into the Infinite Desert!

Additionally, we’ve added some refer a friend bonus unlocks to the game. Simply observe Steam Friends’ scores on the leaderboard to collect the rewards!

[h2]Character Updates[/h2]
Many of the characters in Cubed and Dangerous have been updated. We wanted them to have more unique traits, so each character has been given something to make it stand out, and we've also added brand new art to them all. There are also two new characters to unlock!

[h2]Bug Fixes and Improvements[/h2]

[list]
[*] Lots of small visual improvements - lighting, character/enemy models, explosions, the floor and more have been incrementally adjusted and improved
[*] Some significant CPU performance improvements by cutting down on redundant physics entities being simulated
[*] Some big performance improvements for Steam Deck (including input polling)
[*] Added the ability to hover over your unboxed loot and check it all out before going to the inventory screen
[*] The Pirate Hat will now show item crates as well as gold bags on the minimap
[*] Fix an issue where the Energy Shield could get stuck on
[*] Fix Three Ninjas airborne movement to look smoother
[/list]

If you've enjoyed this game so far, please remember to leave a review! It's the best way to support indie games on Steam and would be very helpful to us. Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Content Update 1 - Patch Notes
notes.content:
Hey everyone! We’re two weeks post-launch and we’re putting out the first large update, aimed at improving balance and adding more variety. We’re continuing to polish and improve the game every day, and this patch also includes some visual improvements as well as fixes for a few small bugs reported to us.

We're glad you're enjoying the game and hope you enjoy the new patch!

[h2]New Content[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added 2 new minibosses to fight during the campaign
[*] Added 2 new Weapons
[*] Added 4 new Tacticals
[*] Added 1 new Perk to support Flamethrowers a bit more
[*] Items near the portal are now vacuumed up when you enter the portal without collecting them! Fear not, you can panic portal now.
[*] Added a simple visual effect for knockback and fast movement
[*] Added a simple visual effect for stunned enemies
[*] Added a Crown to visually differentiate Elite enemies more strongly
[*] Lots of small UI changes
[*] Restrict the visuals for challenge unlocks for weapons to the Collection page for now
[*] Some players were confused about the foil/border upgrades and whether they had in-game effects - we are planning future changes to these!
[*] Towns are now named “Supply and Demand” to be more consistent with our naming scheme 😛
[/list]

[h2]Balance Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Perks were a little too widely available and it was quite easy to find lots of what you wanted. As an improvement for this we’ve consolidated Epic Perks with the Rare Perk pool, and adjusted the rate at which Perks are found.
[*] Critical Acclaim got hit with the nerf bat. It was too frequently an auto-pick for crit builds.
[*] Elite health pools were a little unbalanced, with the Elite variants of some easier enemies just melting. The HP calculation for Elites now adds some base HP to make sure Elite Pawns are still threats and not just free loot.
[*] Some weapons that were DPS outliers have been tuned - Gun Drones, Cluster Launcher, Chain Gun and the Tornado Cannon have been recalculated to be more in-line with other weapons.
[*] The campaign length has been reduced a little, to make sure each run feels fresh and achievable.
[*] Default difficulty has been reduced in a few areas to help onboarding and early campaigns with no Cube-ulative Challenges™ active.
[*] Heavy Ordinance has been adjusted - it is now Rare, and now reloads faster with a slightly smaller AOE. This is to complement a new legendary Tactical.
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Chuck Twins now have a little bit more graphical variation
[*] Drones now flip upside down less often
[*] Fixed an issue with the button hints blocking mouse cursors
[*] Fixed an issue with Unique Perks being able to be taken more than once if you stacked up boxes
[*] Improve some Unity issues with input drops when at low framerates
[*] The energy wheel no longer warps when characters turn around o_O
[/list]

notes.title: Big Demo Patch!
notes.content:
With more players playing Cubed and Dangerous, we're also starting to get more feedback, and with more feedback comes more patches. We've made a bunch of improvements to the game based on what we've heard from players and also fixed a few issues that people encountered.

Two of the bigger changes are - 1) some adjustments to the Act 1 boss mechanics to make it a little less awkward to line up your shots; and 2) making the Tornado Cannon feel a lot smoother by simply making it auto-fire when fully charged. We also added a feature to be able to swap primary and secondary weapons with a single button press, which was a little clunky to do otherwise.

Full Patch Notes

Content
- Added 1 more Progressive Challenge level
- Added burn modifier rolls to Flamethrowers
- Added visual effect for Flamethrower burns
- Added 1 new Easter Egg item
- Enabled swapping primary and secondary weapons with Y or right-click
- Made some significant shader performance improvements
- Many, many small visual updates and improvements

Balance
- Tornado Cannon now fires automatically at maximum charge, making it easier to wield effectively
- Added some rotation for the block ring for the Ringleader. This should make lining up your shots a bit less frustrating.
- Added a new and complementary rock wall formation to the Ringleader
- Reduced single-hit damage for Spiral Laser, as it has a tendency to one-shot things a little too easily
- Reduced knockback for Honed Laser, as it is much faster firing than Spiral Laser
- Changed Hurts More from 15% to 10% Damage bonus, bringing it more in line with other perks
- Tuned down Soul Ignition's secondary stat magnitudes a little
- Reduced the Stalker main weapon range to reduce cases of getting off-screened

Bugfixes
- Improved accuracy for gamepad crosshairs
- Shifted Vendors out further from the houses so they are easier to see
- Reduced Vendor NPC pushing strength, so they can't push you into corners
- Fixed a bug where shop prices could go negative with enough price reduction
- Fixed some issues with enemies flopping over instead of moving forward
- Fixed some issues with the player character moving strangely when tipped over
- Fixed Bricks to face the player correctly and space more accurately
- Fixed an issue where Rock Wizards could transform themselves into other enemies

notes.title: Demo Updated
notes.content:
Thanks everyone for playing the demo so far. We've had a blast working on it and are so happy to see players out there enjoying it. There's been a lot of great feedback from players that we wanted to get incorporated into some demo updates as soon as we could to give everyone a chance to check them out.

Among the feedback we received there were two areas in particular that were fairly common:

[i]"The Escort Mission is just not as fun as the other ones"[/i]
We've heard it and we definitely agree with you. The mechanics of this mission were detracting from what makes the game as exciting to play as it is, particularly the reflected damage from the V.I.C. to the player and the lack of in-game hints and directions in this mode.

We've decided to remove it for now, so runs will be focused more around our other game modes which received more of the positive feedback.

We'll also be brainstorming a bit (suggestions welcome!) on how to build out a game mode that can use some of the ideas of this but focus on more engaging gameplay.

[i]"Getting a lot of items is great, but opening the boxes was confusing / slow / out of the way"[/i]
We've changed the way items are unboxed with a new flow that should improve time-to-action while drawing attention to items you've acquired, and streamlining the process a little.

We plan on continuing to iterate on the effects and some of the behavior, but wanted to get a first idea in front of demo enjoyers to get more feedback around and see where we can go from there.

[i]A conglomeration of other unrelated feedback[/i]
We've made some visual changes and consistency fixes around visual effects that are all fairly minor but targeted some other areas of feedback as well. 

Additionally we have plans for some more gameplay options to help players tailor their own experiences further than some of the auto detected features (more crosshair options, crosshairs for gamepad as an option, etc), but we want to spend some more time figuring out the design we like for these things moving forward before we put them into the demo.

Thanks again for playing the game so far, and for all your feedback.

We also encourage everyone to provide more feedback as they see fit.  We've added a discussion section to the community hub for feedback if that's your preferred submission, or you can tag us on Twitter/X with your feedback as well.

notes.title: New Demo Update Coming Soon
notes.content:
We're excited to wrap up our first Steam festival today, with some news and a sincere thank you to all the players who have enjoyed the demo so far!

We've had a great time chatting with many of you, and appreciate all the feedback we've received for the demo so far.  Based on this feedback we have a few exciting changes coming to Cubed and Dangerous:
- Escort levels will be swapped for a new level type
- Item collection and unboxing will be streamlined and bring additional visual effects
- Escalation progression will have a clearer cause and effect
- Many more improvements, and maybe a surprise or two, stay tuned for updates
